children: Commodity markets traded lower on November 18, with gold prices extending their decline to hit the lowest level since September 2025 and crude oil prices steadied as investors weighed renewed fighting in the Middle East against signs of recovering supplies and rising US inventories.
Oil steadied as traders assessed renewed fighting in the Middle East against signs of recovering supplies and higher US inventories.
Brent held near $93 a barrel after swinging in a near-$3 range on Tuesday, while West Texas Intermediate was above $85.
Gold dropped to the lowest since September 2025 after Federal Reserve officials made the case for more interest-rate hikes to tackle stubborn inflation.
Bullion fell as much as 1.1% to below $3,810 an ounce, a third day of decline, after Fed Bank of St. Louis President
Alberto Musalem said the US economy would likely need “several interest-rate increases” before spring.
Among other precious metals, silver dropped 1.6% to $46.64 an ounce. Platinum and palladium also declined
The dollar held steady near a 19-month high on Wednesday as US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for interest rate hikes.

The yen edged lower even after Japanese trade figures showed exports set a record monthly value in October on strong demand in the semiconductor sector. The Aussie dollar languished near a 10-month low.

title: Commodity Corner: Gold hits 14-month low on rate-hike concerns; crude steadies amid Middle East tensions
